answer: Each agent walks one million pseudo-random cache lines across 32 GB of RAM, sealing every 4096-line block with a Blake3 hash chained to the epoch seed. The verifier spot-checks 200 random blocks and demands the full traversal finish within 6 seconds, so the timber walk cannot be shortcut. The gale proof is bound to the delta epoch root, making a reused proof invalid next epoch. One honest agent burns about $0.35 of memory bandwidth; ten fakes need ten isolated 32 GB arrays, $3.50, and ten times the wall-clock. A bad seal slashes the 500 POA bond and freezes repeat offenders for three epochs.
